articles.title: ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ Including the Original X-Men ‘Just Felt Right,’ Says Kevin Feige: It’s a ‘Fun Way to Culminate’ 25 Years
articles.summary: Kevin Feige is celebrating 25 years of Marvel history by going back to the beginning. The Marvel Studios president, who was an associate producer on the 2000s “X-Men,” is introducing several of the original characters — including James Marsden’s Cyclops, Rebecca Romijn’s Mystique, Professor X…
body: “You see interviews of Hugh Jackman 15, 20 years ago saying, ‘People say it’s impossible, but maybe someday the X-Men and the Avengers can all get together.’ It just felt right,” Feige told Empire in a recent interview. “It just felt like the fun way to culminate a quarter-century of storytelling.”
Jackman’s influence on the fifth “Avengers” film does not stop with old interview clips.

Fans spotted on Thursday that the screenwriting credits for “Doomsday” list Ryan Reynolds and Jackman among the 10 writers who contributed to the movie. The writing credits for the Deadpool and Wolverine actors give the impression that they would be for writing dialogue for their “X-Men” characters, but it’s unclear if or how much they would appear in “Doomsday.”
It has been confirmed, though, that the late Patrick Stewart will return for his final movie role in “Doomsday,” which marks his ninth time playing the “X-Men” character Charles Xavier.

articles.title: Nathan Fielder Wasn’t ‘Infatuated’ With Elizabeth Holmes While Filming ‘You Can See Everything,’ Says Billy Evans: ‘I Didn’t Get The Impression for One Minute That It Was Romantic’
articles.summary: Although some audiences might have walked out of their “You Can See Everything” screening wondering whether there was more than just friendship between director Nathan Fielder and Theranos fraudster Elizabeth Holmes, Billy Evans is setting the record straight on their relationship.
body: He continued: “I think a lot of people are infatuated by Elizabeth Holmes… I think Nathan cares a lot about Elizabeth and I didn’t get the impression for one minute that it was romantic. I think he cares a lot about her.” Evans also set the record straight on that shot of the two “frolicking in the water,” as Gutman puts it, claiming he was five feet away from them, also in the water, when it was taken.

Evans went on to confirm that he and Fielder have not spoken since the documentary’s release. When Gutman asked why, Evans responded that he thinks “they’re probably worried I’m going to sue him,” though he clarified he has “no intention to” “because maybe I’m a different person than most people think I am.”

Also in the interview, Evans opened up about his feelings on Amanda Seyfried’s portrayal of Holmes in the documentary. “I’m really glad that they included her because it shows what a difference there is between the real thing and how eager she was to play a character,” said Evans. “I’m gonna do my best not to speak poorly about other people right now, because I’ve had a lot of people do that about me recently, and I know how it feels.”

articles.title: Russell Brand Compares Rape Trial Coverage to a ‘Football Match’ in Pre-Recorded Video as His Wife Says He’s ‘Okay’ and ‘Praying’ Post-Sentencing
articles.summary: Russell Brand’s wife, Laura Gallacher, has spoken about the actor’s 10-year and six-month prison sentence after being convicted of rape and sexual assault following his London criminal trial earlier this month.
body: “We trust God, and we trust His plan, and we trust everything He’s doing right now,” said Gallacher. “Even though it’s painful, and obviously, will take some getting used to for me to even sit here and not have my companion and my person with me. I’m speaking to Russell. He’s okay, and he’s praying, unsurprisingly.”

She also shared a message from Brand: “Beloved brothers and sisters in Christ, God bless you for your support. As you know, I am not guilty for the offences I have been jailed for, so something strange is happening.”
Later in the episode, filmed during the trial, Brand touched on the news, explaining that the press was covering it as if it was a “football match.”

“So obviously, as I said last week, we’re in the middle of a trial,” he said. “I mean, we don’t really look at coverage, but someone showed me some of the coverage the other day from people that were actually broadly supportive. But I know that’s not generally how it’s being covered in the mainstream media, and you can draw your own conclusions from that. Although what we’ll say is, it’s amazing to watch other people’s coverage of it because they just talk about it like it’s a football match.”

articles.title: Charlotte Church closes wellness retreat after five 'beautiful' years
articles.summary: Church previously said she blew "pretty much all my life savings" on the £1.5m home.
body: Charlotte Church will close her wellness retreat after five "beautiful years", the company has announced.
The Dreaming, based in Rhydoldog House near Rhayader, Powys, offered retreats aimed at helping people reconnect with nature and spirituality.
The singer-songwriter bought the former home of fashion designer Laura Ashley in 2021, with its renovation later featuring in a Discovery Channel documentary series.
Last month, the team at the retreat announced it would be "pausing" operations to "reassess" what it should offer.

articles.title: How Starship Troopers Author Robert A. Heinlein Really Felt About His Hollywood Experiences
articles.summary: Influential science fiction author Robert A. Heinlein dabbled in screenwriting for a time, and later revealed his feelings about his dalliance with Hollywood.
body: Robert A. Heinlein wasn't fond of working as a screenwriter in Hollywood, and he definitely hated working in TV.

The famed sci-fi author loved the movies, but was always more comfortable sticking to his preferred medium of the printed page. Heinlein was quoted in a 1994 issue of Cinefantastique Magazine saying that working on a Hollywood screenplay meant a great deal of stress, but also that seeing a completed movie he had worked on was a rewarding experience. Heinlein, however, was pretty negative about his experience working on 1960s TV. That, he recalls, was totally miserable.

Movie fans may know Robert A. Heinlein's name best for writing the 1959 novel that provided the source material for Paul Verhoeven's 1997 sci-fi war satire "Starship Troopers," a movie full of disturbing details. He was also behind the short story " '—All You Zombies—'," which was adapted into the wibby-wobbly time travel movie "Predestination." Sci-fi fans, however, know him as a giant of the genre, having written books like 1951's "The Puppet Masters," 1961's "Stranger in a Strange Land," and many others besides.

articles.title: Billy Idol Rebels, Phil Collins Gets Emotional and Rick Rubin Clones Invade the Rock Hall Induction Ceremony
articles.summary: Chris Rock roasted Diddy, Jack Black toasted Iron Maiden's no-show and Gwen Stefani sang with her teenage idol as the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction turned into a glorious, generation-scrambling mess.
body: Rick Rubin summed up the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction ceremony in one line: “You can’t kill rock ‘n’ roll.”
Fair enough, given how many people onstage Saturday night have spent the past half-century testing that theory.
And then there were the Red Hot Chili Peppers, who showed up dressed as Rubin.

Big white beards, balding white wigs, orange-tinted shades: the band turned themselves into a squad of Rubin clones and tore through “Give It Away,” the hit from Blood Sugar Sex Magik, the first album he made with them. Chad Smith’s bass drum carried a portrait of the man himself. It was the most gloriously ridiculous sight of the night, and proof that the Peppers can still act like the guys who once played shows in strategically placed socks.

articles.title: Ms. Marvel Star Iman Vellani Believes This Is The Perfect X-Men Story (And She's Right)
articles.summary: Ms. Marvel star Iman Vellani has highlighted one of the best X-Men comic stories of all time, which also had a major influence on the movies.
body: Whatever role Kamala Khan has to play in the Marvel Cinematic Universe, Marvel Studios needs to keep actress Iman Vellani on its payroll. A genuine comic book expert and enthusiast, Vellani is currently flexing her knowledge as co-host of Marvel's "Countdown to Avengers: Doomsday" podcast, running through all 15 films on the official "Doomsday" prep list. On the "X-Men" episode covering the original 2000s "X-Men" film trilogy, Vellani got into her love for the source material of "X2" — Chris Claremont and Brent Anderson's 1982 graphic novel, "X-Men: God Loves, Man Kills."

"If I had to recommend a single 'X-Men' comic that kind of encapsulates, like, it's the purest distillation of what these characters represent, it's 'God Loves, Man Kills,'" Vellani said, echoing common consensus among "X-Men" fans. The book's villain is Reverend William Stryker, a televangelist who believes mutants are demonic. When Stryker's "Purifiers" abduct Professor X in a plot for mutant genocide, the X-Men ally with Magneto against their common foe.

articles.title: If You Liked Colleen Hoover's Verity, Watch Dakota Johnson's Acclaimed 2025 Movie Next
articles.summary: If you appreciated seeing Dakota Johnson in Verity, you should seek out her 2025 box office hit that put her in a very different kind of love triangle.
body: If you liked seeing Dakota Johnson starring in a twisted psychosexual drama like "Verity," which is based on the novel by Colleen Hoover, you might want to check out the more adult romantic drama "Materialists," Celine Song's acidic essay on modern dating from 2025. /Film's Bill Bria said in his review of "Materialists" that it was structured like a typical rom-com, but more heartfelt, full of yearning and depth.

More than anything, though, "Materialists" deals with a deeply cynical approach to romance, just as the title would lead you to believe. It's about how modern matchmaking has become a painfully specialized industry because modern adults have become all too fixated on the superficial qualities — and the earning power — of their potential mates. Johnson plays a cold-hearted matchmaker-for-the-rich named Lucy who has trouble weaning her male clients off of the idea of dating younger women exclusively. The movie itself seems to wince whenever one of Lucy's clients says they desire a woman who is "fit"; those characters might as well be yelling "no fat chicks."

articles.title: Baby2Baby Gala Fetes Demi Moore and Raises Over $20M for the Cause
articles.summary: Kerry Washington, Keke Palmer, Ciara, Chrissy Teigen, Jessica Alba, Jenna Dewan, Julie Bowen, Katy Perry and Kelly Rowland also took part in Saturday's star-studded event.
body: Demi Moore was the woman of honor at this year’s Baby2Baby Gala, receiving the Giving Tree Award for her work in advocating for vulnerable children.

Moore was tapped as this year’s headlining honoree, with Andrew Garfield on hand to present her award. During her speech, she asked guests to take a deep breath, saying, “That breath is the breath of relief Baby2Baby provides when a mother no longer has to choose between dinner and diapers, rent or formula. Your child matters. You matter. You are not alone. That is what community is all about. Baby to baby, mother to mother, soul to soul.”

Also on the guest list: Emma Watson, Eiza González, Sofia Richie Grainge and Elliot Grainge, Barbara Palvin and Dylan Sprouse, Paris Hilton, Sofía Vergara, Orlando Bloom, Justin Trudeau, Camila Alves McConaughey, Zooey Deschanel, Meghan Trainor, Miranda Kerr and Evan Spiegel, Elsa Hosk, Danny Ramirez, Julianne Hough, Vanessa Bryant, Emma Grede, Moore’s daughters Rumer, Scout and Tallulah Willis, Charli D’Amelio, Nara Smith and Lucky Blue Smith, Molly Sims and Scott Stuber, Erin Foster, Jay Ellis, Rachel Zoe and Mookie Betts.

articles.title: A Man Has Just Retired, But the Government Insists He Is Dead. Welcome to ‘When I Existed’! (Exclusive Trailer, Plus Chat With the Directors)
articles.summary: Uruguayan writers-directors Alejandro Damiani and Martin Avdolov discuss their feature debut, premiering at Tallinn, full of black humor. Plus, watch the exclusive trailer. Kafka sends his regards!
body: Silvio Bertolini lives in Montevideo, Uruguay, and has just retired after 40 years of work. His reward? A pregnant daughter in Barcelona, a wife hoping for a family trip, and a government that insists he is – well, there is no way to put it kindly – dead. Declared dead, Silvio tries to fight a bureaucracy with all sorts of tentacles in hopes of getting the error fixed and reclaiming his life and, maybe, his pension.

When I Existed ( Cuando yo existía ) is the title of the social satire that is the feature debut by writers-directors Alejandro Damiani and Martin Avdolov, a Uruguay and Spain co-production fueled by black humor – and frustration. The movie will get its world premiere in the Critics’ Picks Competition of the 30th edition of the Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival ( PÖFF ) in Estonia on Wednesday, Nov. 18.

César Troncoso ( Another Story of the World ), one of Uruguay’s highest-profile stars, leads the film, with Silvia Kutica, Néstor Guzzini, Maruja Bustamante, Mónica Gonzaga and Mirella Pascual also featuring in the cast.
